messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered for gpu-serving.high_queue_growth in eu-west-3 — queue depth 18,400, p95 latency 3.4s. Paging matt (oncall).

matt (oncall): ack, looking.

matt (oncall): quick triage — queues spiking across multiple GPU pools in eu-west-3, autoscaler logs show scale-ups suppressed and a bunch of cloud errors. Customers seeing 500s/timeout.

diego (infra): looking at autoscaler: 'scale up suppressed: reached max_replicas (50)'. Also seeing cloud API: `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Quota 'GPUS' exceeded for project'` — so two things: driver/runtime flapping + quota limit hit.

kyle (runtime): fyi runtime logs show repeated CUDA/Xid errors followed by driver pod OOMs. snippets from node-42 dmesg:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 156, PID=2222 Thu Mar 12 12:34:56 2026
[ 1234.568012] nvidia: GPU assert: client killed, context lost
[ 1238.901234] kubelet: kubelet killing container "runtime" due to OOMKilled
```

matt (oncall): impact? which customers affected? any premium SLAs at risk?

eva (support): Customer reports: "embedding API returns 500s and huge queues, some fallback to CPU also timed out" — we have 3 customers flagged as high tier with increased error rates. Support bridge open.

diego (infra): autoscaler behaviour: when nodes start flapping (Ready -> NotReady) the cluster records them unhealthy and doesn't scale because MaxReplicas was hit earlier attempting to replenish. So effective GPU capacity is lower than expected. Cloud quota prevents adding more GPUs. I've opened quota ticket but ETA 4-6 hrs.

kyle (runtime): mitigation suggestion: cordon+drain the most noisy/flapping nodes, restart driver daemonset on the remaining nodes to stop Xid churn. Also disable autoscaler burst to avoid spinning up nodes that immediately crash and consume quota.

matt (oncall): doing cordon/drain on node-42 and node-43 now, then restart driver. I'll also enable temporary CPU-fallback for non-SLA customers to reduce pressure.

matt (oncall): commands I ran:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-42
kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/gpu-driver -n infra
```

diego (infra): thanks. I'm temporarily increasing autoscaler max_replicas from 50 -> 70 (soft change) to allow scale while we sort quota; will hold creation until driver stability confirmed. Also moving low-priority batch jobs out of eu-west-3 to eu-central-1.

kyle (runtime): after restart, driver on node-42 shows no more Xid 156. node-43 still flapping; logs indicate kernel driver v0.9.7b introduced a memory spike under specific seq_len patterns.

matt (oncall): node-43 cordoned, draining. Replaced node-43 (recreate instance). New node joins Ready.

eva (support): notifying impacted customers: posting support status and adding "degraded performance" to status page. Messaging: "We are experiencing degraded GPU performance in eu-west-3; engineers are actively mitigating; some requests may fall back to CPU or be delayed. ETA next update 30 mins."

incident-bot: Incident created INC-2026-3244. Channel #inc-INC-2026-3244 created.

tara (sre): taking handoff from matt in 25m. Please leave notes and any followups.

diego (infra): cloud quota increase requested (case #CLOUD-98765). If approved we can spin new GPUs in 30-45m. Until then we'll rely on reclaimed nodes + CPU fallbacks.

kyle (runtime): temporary workaround: pin driver to v0.9.6-rc until we roll a fix; I'll prepare a canary rollout for the daemonset. Suggest adding kernel-level Xid backoff: auto-restart only after backoff to avoid crash loops.

matt (oncall): done — rolled back driver daemonset to v0.9.6 on a canary set. Observing reduced OOMs. Queues dropping from 18k -> 6k in last 12 minutes. Error rate for top customers falling.

eva (support): Customer A confirmed latencies improving, still seeing some 5xxs, they've paused non-essential requests. Customer B asked for SLA credit if this persists.

tara (sre): taking over active duties. Matt — leave your runbook notes in the incident channel. I'll keep pager open until quota or full capacity restored.

matt (oncall): handoff complete. Key actions logged: cordon/drain 2 flapping nodes, rollback driver to v0.9.6 canary, temporarily raised autoscaler soft limit, moved batch jobs, enabled CPU fallback for non-SLA traffic, support notifications sent.

kyle (runtime): next steps: prepare postmortem, root cause appears to be driver regression (v0.9.7b) triggering memory blowups under particular tokenization/sequence patterns; recommend pinning driver version in staging, add extra healthprobe to daemonset, and add fallback cross-region spill policy to autoscaler so quota exhaustion in one region spills to another automatically.

diego (infra): I'll follow up on cloud quota case and schedule node replacements for any previously flapping hardware.

eva (support): I'll track customer escalations and collect error samples for the postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3244 status -> mitigated (degraded performance persists but error rates dropping).

tara (sre): leaving a note: postmortem required. Owner: kyle (runtime). Target OR for postmortem within 72h.

matt (oncall): thanks team. Handoff complete to tara.

eva (support): closing support bridge; will re-open if customers report regression.

-- end of thread --
